title: Circuits for polynomial-time verifiers
statement: For every Boolean predicate $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$, if the verifier associated to $M$ is efficient in the polynomial-time verifier model, then there exist natural numbers $A,K$ such that, for every $n$ and every bit string $r$ of length $a(n+1)^k$, there is a well-formed Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits, at most two inputs to each gate, and size at most $A(n+1)^K$, whose output on each $v\in\{0,1\}^n$ equals $M(v,r)$. Here well-formed means that no gate lists an input more than once and every negation gate has exactly one input.
hypotheses_covered: The verifier associated to $M$ is efficient
